title: Eleven Words on a Postcard
subtitle: 危险防范 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 危险防范（灾害防范·危险与逃生）
meta: 主题语境：危险防范（灾害防范·危险与逃生）　|　核心词汇：threat　|　正文 371 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 threat 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: The ① threat came on a postcard, anonymous, in 1974: one sentence, eleven words, saying that the cliff path would be closed and that anybody who walked it after the first of June would be sorry. The policeman who read it said a ② threat to a path is not a threat to a person, and my grandmother said yes it is, and she was right and he was not, and nothing happened for thirty-one years.

There was a ③ threat of rain all that week and the path was wet, and eleven people walked it on the Sunday and one of them did not come back. The cliff, as it turned out, had been ④ posing a threat to the village for a hundred years: the survey that said so had been written in 1961 and filed, and my grandmother had read it in the shop window and remembered it for thirteen years.

In 1975 the path was ⑤ under threat of closure, and the hotel at the top said this would ruin them. A man from the hotel ⑥ made a threat in the shop, in front of eleven people: anybody who closed the path would be sorry. My grandmother wrote it down on the back of a bill, with the date, and put it in a drawer, and eleven years later the police asked her for it.

He never ⑦ carried out the threat, and nothing was ever proved against him. The ⑧ threat, meaning the thing that was actually dangerous, was never the man at all: it was the cliff, which had been going into the sea at eleven centimetres a year since 1800, which nobody measured until 1989, and the threat had been there all along.

In 1994 a ⑨ threat to the road appeared, in the form of a crack eleven metres long, and the road was shut in a week and reopened eleven years later, further inland. The ⑩ threat on the postcard, as it turned out, had been a warning from somebody who knew about the cliff and had no other way of saying it. My grandmother said a threat is sometimes the only form a warning can take, and that a threat you can read is better than a cliff you cannot.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: A. n. 威胁；恐吓（话语或行为）
B. n. 威胁（源）；可能造成危害的人或事物
C. n. 隐患；真正的危险所在
D. 固定搭配：pose a threat to ... 对……构成威胁
E. 固定搭配：under threat（of）面临……的威胁；有……之虞
F. 固定搭配：make / issue a threat 发出威胁
G. 固定搭配：a threat of ... ……的迹象／兆头
H. 固定搭配：carry out a threat 把威胁付诸行动

items.q: The threat came on a postcard, anonymous
a threat to a path is not a threat
There was a threat of rain all that week
had been posing a threat to the village
the path was under threat of closure
a man from the hotel made a threat
He never carried out the threat
The threat, meaning the thing that was actually
a threat to the road appeared
The threat on the postcard, as it turned out

answers.why: the threat 意为“威胁、恐吓”，1974 年一张匿名明信片上写着一句十一个字的威胁。
a threat to a path 意为“对一条小路的威胁（源）”，警察说对小路的威胁不等于对人的威胁。
a threat of rain 意为“要下雨的迹象、兆头”，那一整周都有要下雨的迹象，小路很湿。
pose a threat to ... 意为“对……构成威胁”，那座悬崖一百年来一直对村子构成威胁。
under threat of ... 意为“面临……的威胁、有……之虞”，1975 年那条小路面临被关闭之虞。
make a threat 意为“发出威胁”，旅馆的人当着十一个人的面发出威胁。
carry out a threat 意为“把威胁付诸行动”，他从未把威胁付诸行动。
the threat 意为“真正的隐患、危险所在”，真正的危险根本不是那个人，而是悬崖。
a threat to the road 意为“对公路的威胁（源）”，1994 年出现了对公路的威胁：一条十一米长的裂缝。
the threat 意为“那句威胁（的话）”，明信片上那句威胁其实是一个知情者的警告。

task2.title: Task 2　语境运用
task2.intro: 请把下列句子译成英文，括号里是必须用到的形式。
items: 1974 年一张匿名明信片上写着一句十一个字的威胁。（threat）
那一整周都有要下雨的迹象，小路很湿。（a threat of）
那座悬崖一百年来一直对村子构成威胁。（pose a threat to）
1975 年那条小路面临被关闭之虞，山顶的旅馆说这会毁了他们。（under threat of）
旅馆的一个人当着十一个人的面发出威胁，我祖母把它记了下来。（make a threat）
他从未把威胁付诸行动；真正的隐患是那座悬崖。（carry out a threat）
answers: In 1974 the threat came on an anonymous postcard: one sentence, eleven words.
There was a threat of rain all that week and the path was wet.
The cliff had been posing a threat to the village for a hundred years.
In 1975 the path was under threat of closure, and the hotel at the top said this would ruin them.
A man from the hotel made a threat in front of eleven people, and my grandmother wrote it down.
He never carried out the threat; the real threat was the cliff.

answers: The threat came on an anonymous postcard in 1974, and the policeman who read it said a threat to a path is not a threat to a person.
